newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rockets ahead of new guilder pact.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rockets ahead of new guilder pact.

text.p: Dutch overnight guilders rocketed by 40 basis points to 3.12/25 percent on Thursday as a three-month secured loans pact approached expiry with at least one large bank having used up its quota.

The secured loans pact, expiring on October 18, allows the joint commercial banks to borrow an average 4.36 billion guilders a day frp, the central bank, but some banks have already used up their allowance.
They now need to fund their needs in the interbank market and counterparties, usually smaller banks, are scarce because of a tightly allocated special advances pact.
The special advances allocation is a separate money market instrument used by the central bank to finetune liquidity.
"The allocation of 10 percent of requests is tight and that leaves small banks with no opportunity to make a deal (with a larger bank in need of overnight cash)," one dealer said.
"That situation has driven prices to the offer side of the market," he said.
Usually call money drops at the end of a secured loans pact as banks have "saved" under the pact and use up these reserves.
One bank named three large bidders which were hardly met by offering parties, while another dealer mentioned one large bank in particular.
Prices elsewhere in the market were unchanged and volumes were low.
